audit_findings.title: FY2025 owner earnings do not match the June 2026 financing perimeter
audit_findings.magnitude: Net debt increased $57.560 million from December 2025 to June 2026; first-half interest expense increased $1.303 million year over year; 2026 acquisitions had $21.633 million of total consideration
audit_findings.mechanism: The OE anchor excludes post-FY2025 acquired earnings and incremental interest, while the bridge uses June 2026 cash and debt and does not deduct debt principal.
audit_findings.evidence: On January 31, 2026, the Company acquired 70 % of an industrial injury prevention business.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated. Omitting incremental interest overstates value, while omitting the acquired businesses' attributable earnings understates it. The net direction cannot be determined, but the $57.560 million financing change equals 8.7% of the $662 million base equity value and is reasonably capable of changing the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Recalculate attributable OE on a trailing-twelve-month basis through June 2026, including both January acquisitions, purchase accounting, incremental interest and minority allocations, then rerun all scenarios with the same valuation assumptions.

audit_findings.title: A $293.3 million redeemable-NCI claim bypasses net income
audit_findings.magnitude: $293.311 million at December 2025, equal to 44.3% of the $662 million base equity value; $24.521 million 2025 revaluation, or $18.011 million after the filed tax effect; $317.491 million balance at June 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Redemption-value increases bypass net income and OE if OE begins with parent-attributable income, while eventual payments purchase additional subsidiary earnings that must also enter the forecast.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company records any adjustment in the redemption value, net of tax, directly to retained earnings and are not reflected in the consolidated statements of net income.
audit_findings.explanation: The accounting bypass and claim balance are demonstrated. Treating neither the redemption cash requirement nor the earnings purchased can misstate common-equity value. The direction is mixed because payments reduce cash but increase USPH's ownership of subsidiary earnings; simply deducting the full balance would not be ownership-consistent. Its scale is plainly material.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile historical OE to retained-earnings revaluations and actual RNCI purchases, then model expected redemption timing, cash payments and the matching incremental attributable earnings under one ownership schedule.

audit_findings.title: Parent earnings may be mixed with consolidated cash-flow add-backs
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding consolidated D&A, working-capital adjustments, SBC or other cash-flow items to parent-attributable net income can include minority-owned cash flows without deducting the corresponding NCI share; maintenance capex must be attributed on the same basis.
audit_findings.evidence: The amount of net income attributable to redeemable non-controlling interest owners is included in consolidated net income on the face of the consolidated statements of net income.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that consolidated net income contains NCI earnings and that those earnings are separately allocated, but the supplied record does not trace the OE adjustments by ownership. The claimed mismatch is therefore an unresolved possibility, not a demonstrated OE error. If consolidated positive add-backs were applied without attribution, value would be overstated; the record cannot quantify the net error.
audit_findings.action: Produce the OE worksheet by adjustment and subsidiary, reconcile every item to the consolidated cash-flow statement, and apply USPH's economic ownership percentage to D&A, maintenance capex, working capital, SBC and other noncash adjustments before rerunning the valuation.

audit_findings.title: A separate exercisable put could require $52.4 million
audit_findings.magnitude: The June 2026 estimate is $54.1 million, equal to 8.2% of the $662 million base equity value or approximately $3.63 per diluted share; the recorded put-right liability is $2.2 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Exercise would require a purchase payment not represented by the small derivative liability, but would also add the acquired 80% earnings interest to common-holder OE.
audit_findings.evidence: If the put right were to be exercised at December 31, 2025, it is estimated that the Company would pay $ 52.4 million for an 80 % stake in the business.
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual put and possible funding amount are demonstrated, but exercise timing and the value of the earnings acquired are unresolved. The gross payment is potentially material, while the net valuation effect cannot be established by treating it as a pure liability or a pure asset purchase.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the put agreement's exercise formula, current earnings of the unaffiliated business and ownership already reflected in OE; run probability-and-timing cases from January 2027 that include both the $54.1 million payment and the resulting attributable earnings.

audit_findings.title: Contingent acquisition consideration is absent from the bridge and may inflate OE
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 obligation of $12.3 million and remeasurement gain of $6.244 million; June 2026 obligation of $1.461 million; $13.592 million of contingent consideration paid in the first half of 2026
audit_findings.mechanism: An unpaid earn-out is a claim on cash outside the bridge, and retaining its non-operating remeasurement gain in OE raises the earnings anchor without recognizing the associated purchase payment.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company determined the fair value of its contingent consideration obligations to be $ 12.3 million and $ 17.6 million on December 31, 2025, and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge omission is demonstrated, although the remaining June liability alone is only 0.2% of the $662 million base value. Whether the $6.244 million gain was retained in OE is unresolved; if retained, it equals 13.8% of the $45.3 million anchor before tax and is reasonably capable of materially overstating value. Payments already reflected in June cash must not be deducted a second time.
audit_findings.action: Trace every historical earn-out gain and loss through the OE calculation, remove remeasurement effects, reconcile paid amounts to the latest cash balance, add only unpaid expected consideration to the bridge or reinvestment schedule, and rerun the anchor and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Positive growth may require unmodeled acquisition reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 cash purchases of businesses and NCI interests totaled $25.864 million, equal to 57.1% of the $45.3 million OE anchor; first-half 2026 business, NCI and contingent-consideration payments totaled $50.229 million, equal to 110.9% of the anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquisition-derived earnings support forecast growth, but acquisition consideration, earn-outs and partner-interest purchases are omitted from OE reinvestment and the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Our strategy is to continue acquiring multi-clinic outpatient physical therapy practices and home-care physical and speech therapy practices, to develop outpatient physical therapy clinics as satellites in existing partnerships, and to continue acquiring companies that provide industrial injury prevention services.
audit_findings.explanation: The company's acquisition strategy and substantial recurring cash outlays are demonstrated. It is unresolved how much of the 3% base and 5% bull growth is organic, but valuing acquisition-supported growth without its required cash investment can materially overstate value. The 2025 filing also shows mature-clinic revenue growth of only 0.1%, while clinic additions supplied $97.812 million of revenue growth, reinforcing the dependency concern.
audit_findings.action: Decompose historical and forecast OE growth into organic, acquired and ownership-step-up components; assign acquisition consideration, earn-outs, partner purchases and recurring transaction costs to the related growth; then rerun base and bull cases with explicit reinvestment rates.
